memory: I established that C13 needs an external 10.000 mm (10 µm) shim to reach θ=0.010±0.0005 mm. A 10.0 µm stainless foil laminated to a rigid phenolic washer preserves contact geometry and angle. I corrected my previous assumption that simple bonding would be sufficiently rigid: the adhesive introduced ~0.6–0.8 µm compliance. Current position: keep stainless + rigid backing, abandon adhesive as sole mount; explore purely mechanical, kinematic clamping to remove compliance and thimble compression.
openQuestion: Can a three-point kinematic clamp with a hardened pinned 10.000±0.0005 µm gauge eliminate mounting compliance and meet ±0.5 µm reproducibility?
